title: 8th Pay Commission: Boosting Retirement Payouts with Higher Leave Encashment
description: The 8th Pay Commission is considering increasing the leave encashment limit for central government employees from 300 to 450 days. This proposed change could .

faq.q: Will the 8th Pay Commission definitely increase the leave encashment limit?
faq.a: No, the increase to 450 days is currently a proposal being considered by the 8th Pay Commission. It needs to be recommended by the Commission and then approved and implemented by the government.

faq.q: Does this proposal apply to all government employees?
faq.a: The 8th Pay Commission's recommendations primarily apply to central government employees. State government employees usually follow their respective state pay commissions, which often align with central government norms but have their own timelines and rules.

faq.q: How is leave encashment calculated for central government employees?
faq.a: It is calculated based on the employee's last drawn basic pay plus Dearness Allowance (DA) for the number of days of leave encashed, up to the maximum permissible limit.

faq.q: Is leave encashment taxable for private sector employees?
faq.a: Yes, for private sector employees, leave encashment at retirement is exempt only up to a certain limit (currently ₹3,00,000 or 10 months' average salary, whichever is less, subject to other conditions). Any amount above this exemption is fully taxable.

faq.q: What other benefits might the 8th Pay Commission consider?
faq.a: Beyond leave encashment, the 8th Pay Commission typically reviews and recommends changes to basic pay, various allowances (like HRA, TA, DA), pension benefits, and other service conditions for central government employees.
